summary: PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23 extracts Browning–Le Boudec–Sawin, The Hasse principle for random Fano hypersurfaces (Ann. of Math. 197 (2023); read as arXiv 2006.02356v1, hash reproduced). It has 129 items, 8 routes and 19 source issues. After a full re-read of the paper, with the main estimates recomputed, the item statements are faithful. All nineteen source issues are correct, the six library citations hold at the pin, and no route lands in a finished blueprint. There are six findings, 3 medium and 3 low. (1) The file has no sourceVersions although E3 quotes a stated result. Because its notes say 'the published text … is subscription-only', collation.py counts it as read from the published version and leaves it off the collation worklist. (2) ST.5 of ArithmeticStatistics now plans σ(a;Q), the Veronese vector and Lemma 3.11, which route 7 still sends to the pending Part II design. (3) /pv-density-ball, on which Theorems 1.1 and 2.2 rest after E19, has no proof route, and route 4 never reached ST.2's blueprint. (4) Only a Chebyshev bound is needed for W, not the prime number theorem. (5) The review's route 4 and 5 reasons misattribute σ(a;W) and Lemmas 5.1–5.4. (6) Bhargava's Theorem 2 holds for every region and rests on Bhargava–Skinner, which the item does not record.

There is no errata file research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23.json. cc-f805bf appears in none of the result, the report, the review JSON, the review report, the handoff or the commit messages.

Disclosure. This session red-teamed Browning–Sawin 20 (PR #4792), wrote FIX-RT-AREA-finitefields and FIX-RT-AUDIT-07 (the exponential-sum and sieve audit), and wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-74/80. Finding /3 cites the FF.2 Lang–Weil nodes of the FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums blueprint (PR #2910) and the ST.2 geometric-sieve nodes of BP-ArithmeticStatistics (PR #2864), neither of which is my work. No finding relies on those earlier jobs.

Versions. I downloaded arXiv 2006.02356v1 on 30 September 2026; its SHA-256 210c746b…1efb reproduces the recorded hash. The arXiv abstract page lists only v1 (3 June 2020). Crossref for doi 10.4007/annals.2023.197.3.3 has no update-to, updated-by or relation entry, and the filter updates:10.4007/annals.2023.197.3.3 returns 0 works. The Annals page (HTTP 200) gives Received 5 June 2020, Revised 22 July 2022, pp. 1115–1203 and links no correction. The published text was not obtained, so this red team, like the extraction, is scoped to v1.

The whole paper, read through pdftotext (§§1–5 and the references), with independent recomputation of: Lemma 3.9 from the Smith form; Lemma 3.16's identity det[⟨u_i,u_j⟩²] = 2δ³ (checked at x = e_0, y = e_1) and its constants 1/48 and 2√2 ≤ 3; the d = 2 argument of Lemma 3.15 including (3.17); Lemmas 3.18–3.20 including the log powers; Lemma 3.21's exponent bookkeeping (M^70, M^40, s_1^5s_2^3s_3^3 ≪ Δ^{11/3}); Lemma 3.22's case split; Lemmas 3.23–3.24 (Σe = 20; s_1^25s_2^23s_3^23); Lemmas 4.2–4.3 (constants (N−2)/(N−1) and (N−2)/N); Lemmas 4.5–4.7 and the ranges A ≥ B^{4/5}; Lemma 4.8 including (n−1)(n+1−d) ≥ 4 outside (2,2), (3,3), (4,4); Lemma 4.9's sums G_{>δ} ≪ log A/A^δ + A^{−5/101} and F_{≤δ} with δ = 1/20; Lemmas 4.10–4.11 (partial-summation constants (N−1)/(N−2) and N/(N−2), vol via I and J, the ι normalisation, and the diagonal bookkeeping including the antidiagonal y = −x in Δ^mix and Δ^loc); Proposition 4.1; Lemma 5.1; Lemmas 5.4–5.7; Proposition 5.2 with κ = 1/(4n); Lemmas 5.8–5.10; (5.38) and Proposition 5.3 with κ = 1/n; and the proofs of Theorem 2.2 and Propositions 2.3–2.4.

All 129 items were compared with the text at their locators, statement by statement, including every hypothesis range (n ≥ d rather than n ≥ d+1; the (2,2), (3,3) and (4,4) exclusions; the ranges of A against B; φ ≤ (log A)^{1/2}, φ ≤ A^{3/n} and φ ≤ A). No misstatement was found beyond the corrections the extraction already records.

All nineteen sourceIssues were re-checked at their locators; each is correct. E16's certificate recomputes as 72000/415200 = 30/173. For E13 I recomputed σ(X_0^d; p^r) = p^{r−⌈r/d⌉}(1−p^{−n}). E4's counterexample and E17's homogeneity check both hold. I found no further misprint that is not already recorded. The one other slip in these pages, the missing '#' in Lemma 5.6, is already recorded as ArithmeticStatistics/E641. ArithmeticStatistics/E640 duplicates E11 but carries known = E11, and REGISTER.md lists the mistake once.

Library claims opened at Mathlib 082e2d3: MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (RingTheory/MvPolynomial/Homogeneous.lean:89), IsZLattice (Algebra/Module/ZLattice/Basic.lean:432), ZLattice.covolume (Covolume.lean:72), covolume_eq_measure_fundamentalDomain (:84), covolume_div_covolume_eq_relIndex' (:170) and LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule (LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean:37). All are as the items say.

Missing items searched in declarations.tsv (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474): successive minima, Minkowski's second theorem, transference and Banaszczyk (none; Mathlib has only the first-theorem and number-field Minkowski bounds); Hasse–Minkowski (Tau Ceti has only local predicates such as QuadraticForm.IsLocallyIsotropic in NumberTheory/QuadraticForm/Global/Predicates.lean, so 'planned' at GlobalQuadraticForms layer 5 is right); the prime number theorem (absent; only conditional transfers); primorial_le_four_pow (present, finding /4). The five library and four planned statuses stand.

Planned owners read: atlas stage texts GN.0–GN.6, ST.0–ST.5 and RP.0–RP.6. GN.1 plans Minkowski's first and second theorems and asks for non-full-rank lattices; RP.2 plans adelic points, and its packet lists the proper case X(A) = ∏X(K_v) as remaining. Packets read: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic (77 nodes, first commit 27 September; it plans covolume-projection, covolume-dual, primitive-orthogonal-covolume, successive-minimum and minkowski-second-upper/lower in the owners routes 1–2 name, so there is no conflict); ArithmeticStatistics (415 nodes, 24–27 September; findings /2 and /3); HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions (24 nodes, 27–28 September). All three are partial and were started after the route acceptance on 23 September, so no route lands in a finished blueprint.

Routes and duplication. There is no cycle: the Part II imports GN, ST and RP, and none of them imports it. queue.json: DESIGN-HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII is pending and merges this route with the accepted Part II routes of the DeMarco–Krieger–Ye, DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye, Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger, Gao–Ge–Kühne, Gao–Habegger, Xie–Yuan, Yuan, Harpaz–Wittenberg 20/23 and Skorobogatov–Sofos extractions (the route's reason already separates SS23 by method). Barroero–Widmer, Poonen–Voloch and Ekedahl appear in no other extraction's routes. Lang–Weil is owned at FF.2 and the quantitative Ekedahl sieve at ST.2.

Methods the job asked about. A text scan and the reading show that the paper uses no circle method (it avoids the Hardy–Littlewood main term on p.3), no Deligne or Katz bounds, no Kloosterman refinement, no exponential sums, no Betti-number bounds, no Ekedahl or Bhargava geometric sieve and no Lang–Weil; these enter only through Poonen–Voloch's Theorem 3.6 (finding /3). The averaging over coefficients is a variance bound by geometry of numbers (§§3–4), plus local-factor lower tails (§5). There is no overlap with Browning–Sawin 20's function-field circle method or its owners.

External inputs read. Poonen–Voloch (author PDF, SHA-256 e4ec66ff…c6045): §2, Remark 2.1, Theorem 3.6 and its proof. Le Boudec, arXiv 2006.02288v1 (SHA-256 cb782025…82b8): Theorem 1, which matches /least-lower; Theorem 3; Lemma 3, which matches /primitive-ball-input, with the error term O(T log Y) harmless at Y = 1 because the main term absorbs it. Bhargava, arXiv 1402.1131v1: §1.1, Theorems 1, 2 and 4 (finding /6).

Checks on the other files. The review changed nothing in the extraction. Its route reasons were checked against the route items (finding /5). data/source-issues.json holds each of E1–E19 exactly once.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23.result.json: top level (no sourceVersions); sourceIssues E3 (affects 'a stated result'); interaction with scripts/collation.py
findings.claim: The extraction records a finding that quotes a stated result (E3, against Lemmas 3.19 and 3.20 of arXiv v1) but has no sourceVersions field, which PROTOCOL section 18 requires as soon as any finding quotes a stated result. The version is described only in free text (source.version, source.versionCheck, and each finding's searched list). That free text also misleads the collation tooling. collation.py falls back to the searched/known notes when sourceVersions is absent, and it classifies the reading as 'published' when the notes mention a publisher host and match READ_IT, which includes the phrase 'published text'. Here the notes say 'annals.math.princeton.edu' and 'The published text (revised 22 July 2022) is subscription-only', which says the opposite. So provenance() returns 'published', exposure() skips the paper, and the paper is missing from the collation worklist (research/blueprint/collation/REQUESTS.md), although every quoted statement rests on the 2020 preprint and the 89-page Annals text (revised 22 July 2022) was never compared. The review did not flag the missing field.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL.md section 18: 'the file therefore records what was read, alongside sourceIssues, and scripts/check_errata.py requires it as soon as any finding quotes a stated result'. Running check_errata.versions_checked on the result returns 'sourceVersions is required when a finding quotes a stated result'. The only such finding is E3 ('affects': 'a stated result'). scripts/collation.py:43 READ_IT = re.compile(r"read|collat|sha-?256|offprint|published (pdf|text|version)", re.I); line 68 'if PUBLISHER.search(notes) and READ_IT.search(notes): return "published"'. On this record PUBLISHER matches 'annals.math' and READ_IT matches 'published text', so provenance(record) == 'published' (checked on 30 September 2026). `python3 scripts/collation.py` lists 70 exposed papers and not this one, and REQUESTS.md does not mention it. The extraction's own source.version reads 'arXiv v1, 3 June 2020, 66 pages; not the 89-page published text'. I reproduced SHA-256 210c746b…1efb for arXiv 2006.02356v1 on 30 September 2026, and the Annals page (annals.math.princeton.edu/2023/197-3/p03) gives 'Received: 5 June 2020, Revised: 22 July 2022'.
findings.fix: Add to PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23.result.json: "sourceVersions": [{"kind": "preprint", "url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.02356v1", "read": "2026-09-22", "sha256": "210c746b6b69d466d19a0a90e8f00ca57bf2d4dfb1818b0a9955fe91ae061efb"}], and say in a note that the Annals text (Ann. of Math. 197 (2023) 1115–1203, revised 22 July 2022) was not obtained. With a declared preprint reading, collation.py classifies the record as 'preprint' and lists it for a collation job against the version of record. For the maintainer: the free-text fallback in collation.py treats 'published text … is subscription-only' as a reading of the published text; restrict READ_IT so that a negated or 'not obtained' mention does not count.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23.result.json: item /pv-density-ball (its note and route 4 to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2); research/blueprint/packets/ArithmeticStatistics.json coverage of ST.2
findings.claim: The existence of ρ^loc_{d,n} for the Euclidean ordering is what Theorems 1.1 and 2.2 assert. After E19 it rests on /pv-density-ball, a statement the extraction formulated itself; no source proves it in this form. The item's note says only 'The same sieve over Euclidean balls … gives this form'. It names none of the inputs that Poonen–Voloch's proof of Theorem 3.6 uses, and the Euclidean version needs the same ones: Hensel's lemma from a smooth F_p-point; the Lang–Weil estimate, uniform in the form, which gives an F_p-point when f mod p is absolutely irreducible; the Poonen–Stoll density lemmas (Ekedahl's sieve); and the inequality showing that reducible forms have codimension at least 2, which is exactly where (d,n) = (2,2) is excluded. The route also did not reach its owner. The ArithmeticStatistics blueprint, written after route 4 was accepted, has no ST.2 node for /pv-density, /conic-density or /pv-density-ball. Its ST.2 coverage.remaining lists other papers' accepted routes but not this one, while ST.0 and ST.4 do list this paper's items. As things stand, nothing plans the local-solubility density for the ordering the paper uses.
findings.evidence: Poonen–Voloch, Random Diophantine equations, proof of Theorem 3.6 (author PDF p.3; SHA-256 e4ec66ff…c6045 reproduced on 30 September 2026): 'By Hensel's Lemma, a hypersurface f = 0 will have a point in Q_p if its reduction modulo p has a smooth point in F_p. If f is absolutely irreducible modulo p and p is sufficiently large … the existence of a smooth point in F_p is ensured by the Lang-Weil estimate [LW54]. Lemmas 20 and 21 of [PS99a] will now imply the theorem, provided that we can show that the space of reducible polynomials is of codimension at least 2'. Browning–Le Boudec–Sawin (arXiv v1) p.2: 'If (d, n) ≠ (2, 2), Poonen and Voloch prove [16, Theorem 3.6] that ρ^loc_{d,n} exists'. The suppliers exist: FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2/uniform-lang-weil-estimate and FF.2/lang-weil-estimate, and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve (any compact B ⊂ ℝ^n, codimension k ≥ 1), together with ST.2/lattice-points-on-a-subvariety-in-a-dilated-region. ArithmeticStatistics.json coverage for ST.2: its 'remaining' entries name PAPER-BHARGAVA-GROSS-WANG-17 route 2 and PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21 route 2 but not PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23 route 4. The ST.0 entry lists 'PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23 (family, density, primitive-residue, Floc)', and the ST.4 entry lists route 8.
findings.fix: Rewrite /pv-density-ball's note as a proof route. (i) Real factor: c_∞^{ball} is the normalised spherical measure of the closed cone of real-soluble forms. (ii) For p large and f mod p absolutely irreducible, a smooth F_p-point exists by FF.2/uniform-lang-weil-estimate, and Hensel's lemma lifts it to a Q_p-point. (iii) The forms reducible over F̄_p reduce into a closed subscheme of codimension ≥ 2 when (d,n) ≠ (2,2), by PV's inequality (binom(n+r,n)−1) + (binom(n+d−r,n)−1) ≤ binom(n+d,n)−1−2 for 0 < r < d. (iv) ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve, applied to B = the Euclidean unit ball, gives the uniform tail, and hence the limit c_∞^{ball}∏_p c_p. (v) Möbius inversion gives the restriction to primitive vectors (PV Remark 2.1(2)). Add a ST.2 node for /pv-density-ball, or at least a coverage.remaining entry for route 4 in ArithmeticStatistics.json, that imports these suppliers. Treat /conic-density the same way: Serre's upper bound transfers to the ball by containment B_6(A) ⊂ [−A,A]^6.

findings.claim: The item states log W(B) ~ 3w(B) and says 'The prime number theorem is used', so the Part II design would import the prime number theorem. Every use of (2.12) in the paper needs only W(B) = B^{O(1/log log B)}: in (4.71) and (4.72) (a factor B^{c/log log B}), Lemmas 4.10 and 4.11 (W ≪ A^{c/log log A}), Lemma 5.1 (W^{n+2} ≪ B^{o(1)}) and Proposition 5.2 (W ≪ A). That bound follows from Chebyshev's elementary estimate, which Mathlib has at the pin. The asymptotic log W ~ 3w is itself right, since the primes in (w^{1/2}, w] carry exponent 3, but nothing uses it.
findings.evidence: Paper p.5: 'an application of the prime number theorem reveals that log W ∼ 3w, which implies in particular W ≪ B^{4/log log B} (2.12)'. Uses: p.44 'W ≪ A^{5/log log A}'; p.49 'W ≪ A^{8/log log A}'; p.50 (4.71)–(4.72); p.52 end of the proof of Lemma 5.1; p.57 'The upper bound (2.12) and the assumption φ(A) ≤ A ensure that W ≪ A'. Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Primorial.lean:141 'theorem primorial_le_four_pow (n : ℕ) : n# ≤ 4 ^ n' (alias primorial_le_4_pow at :146). From it, θ(w) ≤ w log 4 and π(w) log w ≤ √w log w + 2θ(w). Hence log W = Σ_{p≤w}(⌈log w/log p⌉+1) log p ≤ π(w) log w + 2θ(w) ≤ √w log w + 4 log 4 · w, so W ≤ B^{6/log log B} for large B. At the pins, declarations.tsv has no unconditional prime number theorem; Tau Ceti has only conditional transfers such as TauCeti.primeTheta_asymptotic_of_primePsi.
findings.fix: Split /W-bound. The consumed statement is: for B large, W(B) ≤ B^{C/log log B} with an absolute C (C = 6 works), proved from Mathlib's primorial_le_four_pow. Add a note that the paper's log W ~ 3w (needs the prime number theorem) is not used. Replace 4 by the constant proved wherever (2.12) is used; nothing downstream depends on its value.

findings.claim: The item states Bhargava's Theorem 2 only for coefficient boxes ('ordered by the maximum of their coefficients'). Its note says the original was not read and that the Euclidean ordering needs the inscribed box [−A/√20, A/√20]^20. Theorem 2 holds for every compact region B that is the closure of an open set containing 0, so the Euclidean ball is covered directly. The note also omits the input the theorem rests on: Bhargava's proof of Theorem 2 uses Bhargava–Skinner's theorem that a positive proportion of elliptic curves over Q have rank 1, fed through the 3-Selmer parametrisation by ternary cubic forms. The route-8 owner, ST.4, lists the item as 'source not yet acquired', so the planner has no statement of what it must import.
findings.evidence: Bhargava, arXiv:1402.1131v1, §1.1 p.2: 'Let B be any compact region in V(R) that is the closure of an open set containing the origin 0 … Theorem 2 For any B, we have lim inf_{t→∞} N_sol(V,t,B)/N_tot(V,t,B) > 0.' (p.3). p.5: 'To prove Theorem 2 … In joint work with Skinner [10], we recently proved: Theorem 4 When ordered by height, a positive proportion of elliptic curves E over Q have rank 1.' p.11: 'Theorem 2 then follows by the identical arguments, but using Theorem 11 instead'. Read on 30 September 2026. ArithmeticStatistics.json ST.4 coverage: 'PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23 route 8 (accepted): … Theorem 2 — source not yet acquired.'
findings.fix: Restate /bhargava-plane-cubics as: 'For every compact region B ⊂ R^10 that is the closure of an open set containing 0, liminf_{t→∞} #{integral ternary cubic forms in tB with a nontrivial rational zero}/#{integral forms in tB} > 0' (Bhargava, arXiv:1402.1131v1, Theorem 2). In the note, record its inputs, Bhargava–Skinner (a positive proportion of E/Q ordered by height have rank 1) and the ternary-cubic parametrisation of 3-Selmer elements, so that ST.4 can plan or import them. Drop the inscribed-box remark, or keep it only as an alternative.
